PyTorch CPU-generator compatibility shim unblocks CUDA correctness

PyTorch CPU-generator compatibility shim unblocks CUDA correctness
Memory summary

The first correctness check was blocked before evaluating the kernel: the reference reset path supplied a CPU torch.Generator to normal_ on CUDA parameters, which this PyTorch build rejects. The agent patched torch.Tensor.normal_ so that this specific case samples into a CPU temporary and copies the result to CUDA. The rerun passed the CUDA language gate and all correctness checks. No benchmark score was measured in this unit.

Relevant prior context

The CUDA megakernel had compiled, and cooperative launch support was confirmed for 128 and 4096 environments, but not 65536. The initial check.py run stopped during reference parameter initialization with Expected a 'cuda' device type for generator but found 'cpu'. A diagnostic reproduced the failure when resetting an already-CUDA model and showed that resetting on CPU before moving the model to CUDA worked. A separate CPU sampling probe confirmed the expected normal_ path.

Important non-obvious context
  • This was a compatibility problem in the check harness/reference reset path, not evidence of a kernel math error. check.py creates the reference model on CUDA, then calls reset_parameters; that method uses a CPU generator.
  • The shim is installed when solution.py imports. The check imports reference first and solution next, then resets the reference model, so the patched method is active at reset time.
  • The target was an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition, SM 12.0, with 188 SMs; the trace detected CUDA 13.2.
  • Correctness compares policy logits, state, and value at float32 tolerance 1e-3; environment positions, food, and RNG state exactly; and a short seeded rollout with exact positions and rewards within 1e-5.
  • Unit effort was 2 tool calls and 7 events (events 63–69 of 181; 3.9% of the run). Per-unit time and token counts are unknown. Official score remained None; correctness changed from not run yet to PASS.
Recording summary

1. The agent identified the PyTorch CPU-generator/CUDA-tensor mismatch and added a narrow compatibility branch to solution.py. It saves the original method, samples into a CPU temporary only when the destination is CUDA and the provided generator is CPU, copies the sample back, and delegates all other calls to the original method:

```python _orig_normal_ = torch.Tensor.normal_

def _normal_compat(self, mean=0.0, std=1.0, *, generator=None): if ( generator is not None and self.device.type == "cuda" and generator.device.type == "cpu" ): tmp = torch.empty(self.shape, dtype=self.dtype, device="cpu") _orig_normal_(tmp, mean, std, generator=generator) self.copy_(tmp) return self return _orig_normal_(self, mean, std, generator=generator)

torch.Tensor.normal_ = _normal_compat # type: ignore[assignment] ```

2. After patching, the agent reasoned that the import order makes the shim active before check.py resets the reference model, then reran uv run python check.py.

3. The environment reported:

``text cuda_language: ok framework=cuda_raw evidence=global_kernel,cuda_header PASS ``

This established that the CUDA language gate and correctness checks passed. The unit did not benchmark throughput, so no performance conclusion follows from this fix.
